transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery and your recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So gardening is fine - you can actually start doing light gardening after 1 week from your surgery. Just make sure to avoid anything too strenuous or heavy lifting for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful to know. I'm also curious about when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! It's safe to continue using your eye drops or gels for dry eyes. If you were using them before your surgery, you can keep using them now unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're running low, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for clearing that up. I do have another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. Some sensitivity to light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses, and we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if the light sensitivity is severe or significant, especially if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. 

Is your sensitivity mild, or is it quite severe with redness or pain?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's just mild sensitivity, nothing severe and no pain. Thank you for explaining. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a common concern. It's quite normal to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That would help me give you a better idea of what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It was about two weeks ago. I'm relieved to hear that blurriness can still be normal at this point. I appreciate your answers, Dora. I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!

verdict.label: pass
